tags.description: Creates a new instance of a class. The class name goes in braces; constructor arguments use §A. Use §NEW{ClassName} §/NEW for zero-argument constructors.
Declares a variable binding. Use ~ prefix for mutable variables. Immutable by default. Give null an explicit existing nullable type, such as ?str.
Defines a standalone function (not a class member). Use for top-level functions or static utility methods.
tags.csharpEquivalent:
public static int Add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
private void Log(string message) { Console.WriteLine(message); }

tags.description: Defines an async function. Use §AF for standalone async functions, §AMT for async class methods.
tags.csharpEquivalent:
public async Task<string> FetchDataAsync() { ... }
public async Task ProcessAsync() { await DoWork(); }

tags.description: Defines a named module for static members. Its functions use §F; C# callers keep the original static class name. Static class declarations with §CL are rejected.
Defines a method within a class. Supports visibility (pub/priv/prot) and modifiers such as virt/vr, over/ov, abs, stat/st, and seal.
Defines an async class method.

tags.open: Inline (type:name) parameters in function headers; indented §I{type:name} for delegates and full indexers
tags.description: Header parameter syntax. Modifiers: 'this' (extension method), 'ref', 'out', 'in', 'params'. Default values use =expr in the signature.
tags.csharpEquivalent: Type name, this Type name, ref Type name, params Type[] name, Type name = default

tags.open: Inline -> type in function headers; indented §O{type} for delegates
tags.description: Declares the return type of a function or method via the header arrow.
Returns a value from a function or method. Use bare §R for void returns.
Defines a class. Supports modifiers such as abs, seal, partial, stat, struct, and readonly. Use §EXT for base class and §IMPL for interfaces.
Specifies the base class for inheritance.
Specifies an interface the class implements.
Defines an interface with method signatures.
tags.csharpEquivalent: public interface IRepository { void Save(Entity e); }

tags.description: For loop with an inclusive integer range. The body is indented under the loop header.
Executes body while condition is true.
Runs the indented body at least once; the matching closer carries the condition.
Conditional branching. §EI for else-if, §EL for else. Both are optional.
Else-if branch in a conditional.
Else branch in a conditional.
Awaits an asynchronous operation.
tags.csharpEquivalent:
var result = await FetchAsync();
await Task.Delay(1000);

tags.description: Exception handling. §TR for try block, §CA for catch (with optional type and variable), §FI for finally.
Catches exceptions. Type and variable name are optional.
Finally block that always executes.
Throws an exception. Use §RT to rethrow in a catch block.
Jump to a specific case label or to the default case in a switch statement. For regular goto, use §GOTO{labelName}.

Declares side effects a function may have. Common effects: cw (console write), db (database), net (network), fs:r/fs:w (file system), rand (random), time, and env. Unresolved external effects are not purity proofs; supply authoritative effect metadata rather than inventing an effect code.
Declares a precondition that must be true when the function is called. Part of Design by Contract.
Declares a postcondition that will be true when the function returns. Use result to refer to the return value.
Defines a property with optional getter and setter. Auto-properties use accessor shorthand such as get,set, get,priset, or get,init. Full properties use indented §GET and §SET bodies.
Property getter.
Property setter with optional visibility modifier.
tags.csharpEquivalent: set { body } or private set { body }

tags.description: Defines a field in a class. Usually private, prefixed with underscore by convention.
Defines a class constructor. Use §BASE with §A arguments to call a base constructor, or §THIS to chain constructors.
tags.csharpEquivalent:
public User(string name) { _name = name; }
public Admin(string name) : base(name) { }

tags.description: Calls the base class constructor.
Chains to another constructor in the same class.
Defines an enumeration. Enum values are indented under §EN and may use = for explicit values.
tags.csharpEquivalent:
public enum Status { Active, Inactive, Pending }
public enum Priority : byte { Low = 0, High = 1 }

tags.description: Defines an event. Simple form has no body. For custom add/remove accessors, use indented §EADD and §EREM blocks inside the event body.
Custom add accessor body inside an event definition (§EVT). Contains statements executed when a handler is subscribed.
Custom remove accessor body inside an event definition (§EVT). Contains statements executed when a handler is unsubscribed.

Creates an anonymous function using name:type parameter pairs. It can capture variables from its enclosing scope. The closing delimiter carries no source ID. Bind local helpers as lambdas, not nested §F declarations. Automatic local-function conversion lowers noncapturing, non-generic direct same-point calls with ordinary parameters. Direct self-recursion also requires a complete proof of pure built-in scalar operations and captures only the initialized internal self binding; unsupported cases remain explicit converter preservation.
tags.csharpEquivalent:
x => x * 2
(a, b) => a + b
items.Where(x => x > 5)

tags.open: §W expression with indented §K pattern → result cases; use in an expression context, such as §R §W
tags.description: Pattern matching switch expression. §K introduces each case/pattern. Use _ for default.
tags.csharpEquivalent:
x switch { 1 => "one", 2 => "two", _ => "other" }
shape switch { Circle c => c.Area(), Rectangle r => r.Width * r.Height }

tags.description: A case in a switch expression. Use _ for default.
Loop control statements.
Continues to next loop iteration.
Resource management with automatic disposal.
tags.csharpEquivalent:
using (var stream = File.OpenRead(path)) { ... }
using var connection = new SqlConnection(connStr);

tags.description: Constraint on a generic type parameter.
Legacy null-coalescing syntax. Prefer Lisp-style (?? left right) for null-coalescing.
Null-conditional member access in Lisp prefix notation. Returns null if target is null, otherwise accesses Member.
Builds an interpolated string from literal parts and §EXP expression parts. Strings are opaque — expressions cannot be embedded inside quotes. Use separate "literal" and §EXP expr parts.
Calls a method or function. Each argument uses §A; §/C delimits nested argument lists.
Imports a namespace or creates an alias. Must appear inside a module (§M{Name}) block.
tags.csharpEquivalent: using Namespace; or using Alias = Namespace;

tags.description: Creates and initializes a fixed-size array. The element type is specified in the header. Elements are space-separated between the opening and closing tags. Supports both explicit (new int[] { ... }) and bare ({ ... }) initializer syntax.
Creates a dynamic list.
tags.csharpEquivalent: new List<Type>() or new List<Type> { elements }

tags.description: Creates a dictionary/map.
Prints to console with newline. Use §Pf for no newline.
Iterates over each element in a collection. Type is inferred in §EACH{variable}; §EACH{variable:type} specifies it explicitly. An optional third field names the index.
Declares an invariant at module scope.

Conditional compilation blocks use §PP for #if and §PPE for #else. Indented statement bodies end at dedent. Nested §PP blocks express #elif. Code inside is conditionally included based on defined symbols.
Declare a mutable binding with a ~-prefixed name; use §ASSIGN for all updates, including increments and compound arithmetic.
Defines an indexer on a class or interface. Full indexers use indented §I parameters and §GET/§SET/§INIT bodies. Compact auto-indexers use accessor shorthand and inline parameters.

tags.open: §DEL{name} with indented §I parameters and optional §O return type
tags.description: Defines a delegate type (function signature). Use for callbacks, event handlers, and function references. §DEL can appear at the top level or nested inside §CL class bodies.
Defines an operator overload for a class or struct. Supports binary operators (+, -, *, /, ==, etc.), unary operators (-, !, ~, ++, --), and conversion operators (implicit, explicit).
Rethrows the current exception in a catch block.
Captures a value into a variable in pattern matching.
Adds a guard condition to a pattern match case.
Marks an argument in inline calls or constructors.
Inline example or test code in documentation.
Documents the version when a feature was introduced.
Marks code as deprecated with a reason.
Documents a breaking change in the API.
Documents an assumption that must be true at this point in the code.
Locks an object while executing the indented body.
Defines a property-based test.
Defines extension methods for an enum type.
Represents a range value (start..end) for array/span slicing.
Indexes from the end of a collection. Equivalent to C#'s ^n operator.

closingTagRules: Structural blocks end at dedent. Calls, block lambdas, do-while conditions and value literals use their documented delimiters.
